title: Hybrid Job Optimization
description: Engineers ask about cost drivers, performance bottlenecks and optimization opportunities across the pilot workspaces, using system tables plus Spark and job logs. Access: engineering group only.

tables.description: One row per job per workspace for the review period (latest daily snapshot): period and monthly cost, DBUs, runs, failed runs and their cost, retries, avg/max minutes, runtime/cost/CPU trends (second half vs first half), clusters per run, worker CPU/memory/swap, idle node-hours and idle_pct, OOM/spill/lost-executor/error counts (driver logs), shuffle and spill GB and max_skew_ratio (Spark event logs), slow/spilled SQL queries, runtime version, Photon, policy, schedule and data-layout flags, category (top fix type), top_recommendation, secondary_findings, fix_effort, risk_level, risk, owner, est_monthly_savings_usd, est_annual_savings_usd, priority_rank (global) and workspace_rank.
One row per workspace: jobs analyzed, jobs needing action, spend, estimated monthly savings, spend on failed runs, and the top opportunity (job, recommendation, saving).
One row per cluster in the review period: workspace, cluster name and source, job_id, node-hours, idle node-hours (CPU below the idle threshold), idle_pct, cost and estimated idle cost.

Append-only daily metrics per job (metric_date): cost, DBUs, utilization, idle, runs, failures, retries, minutes, log signals, shuffle, spill, skew, SQL signals. Use for trends and before/after comparisons.
Same daily metrics as job_daily_history computed live (last 120 days). Use when history does not cover the period yet.
Runs started per workspace per UTC hour of day in the review period; busy_rank 1 is the busiest hour.
Top 100 slowest SQL queries per workspace in the review period (query history): source type, job_id, duration, bytes read, spilled and shuffled, statement preview.
Parsed driver log lines from Watchtower: cluster_id, log_source (stdout/stderr/log4j), log_level, log_ts, log_msg. Join to ops.v_job_cluster_map on cluster_id for workspace_id, job_id and job_run_id.
Maps cluster_id to workspace_id, job_id, job_run_id and task_key (last 90 days).
Pilot scope: workspace ids and names, review_start, review_end, review_label, review_days.

instructions: Scope is the pilot workspaces and review period in ops.v_scope. 'During the review period' means review_start to review_end; v_job_scorecard_latest already covers exactly that period.
Costs are contract cost in USD: usage x effective list price x our contract multiplier (1.093). Report cost columns, not list_cost columns.
est_monthly_savings_usd and est_annual_savings_usd are conservative estimates normalized to 30 days, not guaranteed savings. Call them estimated.

category is the single top fix type (MEMORY, SPILL, LOST_EXECUTORS, FAILING, MULTI_CLUSTER, OVERSIZED, CPU_BOUND or OK). secondary_findings lists further recommendations (retries, skew, shuffle, slow SQL, data layout, runtime, Photon, policy, schedule, idle, cost-vs-utilization, runtime growth).
priority_rank orders all work (1 = first); workspace_rank orders work within one workspace. Always show workspace_name next to job_name: job IDs repeat across workspaces.
CPU and memory are worker-node percentages. Oversized means p95_cpu below 40 and avg_mem below 50. Idle time is in v_cluster_idle (per cluster) and idle_pct (per job).

Shuffle, spill and skew come from Spark event logs; OOM, spill and lost-executor events come from driver logs; SQL query signals come from query history and cover SQL warehouse and serverless queries only.

'Retries' means extra task attempts (task retries or repairs). 'Runtime trend' and 'cost trend' compare the second half of the review period with the first half (runtime_change_pct, cost_change_pct, p95_cpu_change).
Round money to whole dollars. Mention owner and risk when recommending an action.
sample_questions: Which jobs consumed the most DBUs during the review period?
Which clusters had the highest idle time?
Which jobs had the longest runtime trend?
Which jobs experienced the most failures or retries?
Which workloads have increasing cost but declining utilization?
What jobs generated the largest shuffle volume?
What optimization opportunities are suggested for the highest-cost jobs?
What is the top optimization opportunity in each workspace, with owner and estimated saving?
Which quick wins (low effort, low risk) save the most money?
